rationale: g.remove only printed 'Grid disconnected': the held-key list, the held keys' long-press timers, a fired long-press flag and an in-progress two-key gesture all survived the disconnect, so a timer could fire a long press after the grid was gone and the first tap after reconnecting could resolve as a two-key gesture with the stale key or be swallowed. Disconnect now cancels each held key's timer, clears its long-press flag, empties the (live) held-key table and ends the two-key gesture. No behaviour reproduction exists, by decision: an emulator probe did not reproduce a user-visible effect and the human decided (2026-09-11) to fix defensively; the regression is three Lua units in grid_input_tests.lua (test_grid_input_remove_clears_held_keys_and_cancels_their_timers, test_grid_input_remove_forgets_a_fired_long_press, test_grid_input_remove_ends_a_two_key_gesture_in_progress), all three failing on the unfixed m_grid.lua (logged only 'print(Grid disconnected)', no clock.cancel) and passing with the fix. They replace the characterisation unit test_grid_input_remove_alerts_but_keeps_held_keys_and_timers.
